questions.question: ______ is the process by which rocks are broken down at the Earth’s surface into sediments, clay, soils and substances that are dissolved in water.

__
 
• The **breakdown or dissolution **of **rocks and minerals **on the **Earth's surface **is referred to **as weathering**.
 
• **Carrier of weathering **include water, ice, acids, salts, plants, animals, and **variations in temperature.**
 
• **Rocks break down **by the process **called weathering.**
 
• The **effects of weathering **and **erosion **cannot be **resisted by any rock **on **Earth due to its softness**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **process of removing soil, rock, or dissolved material **from one area on the **Earth's crust **and moving it to **another, where it is deposited, **is known as **erosion**. Erosion differs from weathering, which is a static process.
 
• **Wind-blown dust gathers to form loess**, a clastic **deposit that is primarily silt-sized**. Loess or comparable deposits cover 10% of Earth's land surface.

questions.question: The amoeba pushes out one or more finger-like projections called ______ or false feet for movement and capture of food.

__
 
• A **transient arm-like protrusion **of a **eukaryotic cell membrane **that emerges in the **direction of motion **is known as **a pseudopod **or **pseudopodium**.
 
• **Actin filaments **make up the majority of the **cytoplasm-filled pseudopodia**, which may also **contain microtubules and intermediate filaments**.
 
• **Amoeba's pseudopodia**, or **false feet, **allow for **unlimited movement**.
 
• **These pseudopodia allow **it to **shift shape **and **demonstrate movement**. As a result, **pseudopodia **are referred to as **a fake feet in amoeba**.
 
• Food and water are stored in food and water vacuoles, respectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Simple eukaryotes **like **protists **have **an organelle called the feeding vacuole**, also known as the digesting vacuole. In essence, this organelle is a lysosome.
 
• The **contractile vacuole (CV) complex **is an **osmoregulatory organelle **of **free-living amoebae **and **protozoa, **which controls the intracellular **water balance **by accumulating and expelling excess water out of the cell, allowing cells to survive under hypotonic stress as in pond water.
 
• The **innermost portion **of **an amoeba's cytoplasm **is known as **endoplasm**. It has **more granules **and is **denser**. Additionally, it controls the amount of water inside the cell, which affects where the pseudopodia are located.
